column1: # The printed imsak (12 Nov 2026, before the Ramadan 1448 release, spec §7, O11): e-solat's own imsak, which the monitor's
# fetcher and the rows above leave out, read back from the raw answers the monitor already holds by
# archive/code/imsak/imsak_tables.py (no new fetch) into archive/tables/imsak/my-jakim/<capture>/<zone>-<year>.txt, two columns,
# the printed Subuh (equal on every day to the gated table's Fajr above) and the imsak. Every zone prints imsak = Subuh - 10 on
# every day held, and so does the app since the JAKIM imsak round of 12 Nov 2026: the zone's Subuh as e-solat prints it (for
# its latest point, rounded up) less 10 (Jakim.kt, ImsakFrom.PrintedFajr, with an imsak margin of its own fitted as an end on
# every Subuh above as Subuh - 10 and on these imsak columns), checked here as Im, an end: never after the printed imsak. It
# was the reference point's dawn less 10, the dawn the end of eating keeps (up to 4 min before the Subuh), and so 3-4 min
# before e-solat's imsak at eleven of these tables, held back until this round.
# Perlis (PLS01) prints no precaution: its imsak is its Subuh in 2026, and a minute before it on 141 days of 2027 from
# 8 March (the mirror's 2027 table, not seen on e-solat itself); the app shows no imsak there (JakimZones.kt, imsakMarginSeconds = null), so its
# 2027 column is checked as the end of eating (E): the end shown never after the imsak Perlis prints. Its 2027 days are thus
# counted twice in PLS01's end of eating (here and in the F+E row above), the price of the stricter check; its 2026 imsak is
# the Subuh the F+E row already reads, so that row is left out (below). 2026 is e-solat's year table of 28 Sep 2026; 2027 the
# mirror's (api.waktusolat.app, the copy of e-solat the monitor falls back on) of 1 Nov 2026 (Kota Bharu's and Kuala Lumpur's
# of 2 Nov 2026, that capture being the one that holds all twelve months). Sandakan, Kota Kinabalu and Shah Alam's 2027 is not
# held. These rows read ends alone, so they add no place-day (the gate counts a day by a row reading a start) and must fall on
# days a row above holds. Split as the row above for the same zone and year; the other columns are not read ("-").
# No holdout (review of 48ff2384): that split only follows the row above. Each zone's imsak margin is fitted over these
# rows and every Subuh above, test rows included (the smaller fit, as JAKIM's other margins over both years, Jakim.kt), so
# every imsak cell here is a fitted one (ruling R214, the @fitted line at the foot of this file; until 13 Nov 2026 the stamp
# showed 6,935 in-sample imsak days as held out). A fit on the 2025 rows alone cannot stand: it asks a later margin than
# 2027's Subuh allows (WLY01 +7 s against -125 s), after e-solat's imsak. So no imsak day of JAKIM's is a held-out day, and
# the Ramadan guard (checkStamps -Pramadan, ruling R246) names it as checked in fitted rows only.

column1: # The zone round of 13 Nov 2026 (rulings R225-R229): the 37 zones that hold a city of the app's list and were no unit yet,
# each on its own e-solat year tables, the hand capture of 13 Nov 2026 with the requests the monitor's fetcher makes
# (archive/code/manual/my-jakim/esolat_zones.py): a plain GET for 2026, and for 2027 an HTTP POST of e-solat's own
# date-range form (datestart, dateend): 37 POSTs, 30 answered and 7 NO_RECORD! (each table's first line says GET or POST).
# The 2026 table is the fit row and 2027 the test row (Ramadan 1448 in it), but the margins are over both: a fit on 2026
# alone was EARLY on days of 2027 in five of the thirty zones with a 2027 table (KDH02, KDH04, KDH05, NGS02 and PRK02, one
# to three days each), so every day sets the margins, as in the first thirteen zones. No day of a zone's own table is
# therefore held out: these test rows are in-sample, and so are the towns' rows of my-jakim-cities.tsv, which read the
# same tables at the towns' points and give the LATENESS there, not an independent test. Seven zones have no 2027 table
# on e-solat yet (SBH03, SBH04, SBH05, SBH08, SBH09, SGR02, SGR03: NO_RECORD! to the POST): their 2026 table is held as two
# local copies, January to September the fit row and October to December the test row, as Kemenag's Jakarta, the margins
# over the whole year; with one year held (JakimZones.Zone.oneYear) every margin carries 15 s more to its safe side
# (FORWARD_SECONDS) until 2027 is held and the zone refitted; the monitor asks for their 2027 weekly.
# SBH09's fit copy holds 2026-03-28..31 AS PRINTED: four days e-solat's own table prints LATER than the days either side
# (Subuh and Syuruk 10-11 min later, Zohor 6-7, Asar 19-20, Maghrib 3; Isyak in line). They are never left out (R228 as
# its review round left it): the engine holds those four days' starts to the print, never before it (JakimZones.kt, PrintedLater), and its
# sunrise, end of eating and imsak, which never move later, stand up to 13 min BEFORE the print on those days (SBH09's own
# limit). Where SBH09's table rides beside another zone's the four days ride with it: at SWK09's unit (Kampung
# Patarikan, by the border) a start stood up to 11 (Subuh), 8 (Zohor) and 20 (Asar) min AFTER SWK09's own print on those
# four days (SWK09's own limits say so); on every other day at most 4. Read at each zone's own unit (lat/lon empty): its point the zone's first town in the app's list, its start
# point a fitted effective point, not JAKIM's reference point (which is not held), and in KDH02-KDH06, SGR02 and NGS03
# outside the zone (JakimZones.kt). The towns of every zone are read at their own points in my-jakim-cities.tsv; the
# border places, the named places and the app's cities on no zone's list in my-jakim-envelope.tsv (generated).
